form.label: Routes
form.description: The jumps a permitted flow has actually been seen to make: from a declared entry point to a host, from that host onward, and what is listening where it lands.

search.query: | `riskability_fw_edges` | stats count AS edges | append [| inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | stats count AS ledger, count(eval(coverage_state="no firewall data")) AS nofw] | stats max(edges) AS edges, max(ledger) AS ledger, max(nofw) AS nofw | eval edges = coalesce(edges, 0), ledger = coalesce(ledger, 0), nofw = coalesce(nofw, 0) | eval state = case(edges == 0 AND (ledger == 0 OR nofw == ledger), "unconfigured", edges == 0, "empty", 1=1, "ready")

div.b: No firewall data source has been configured, so there are no routes to draw.
div.span: This page draws the jumps a permitted flow has been seen to make, from the firewall's own logs. Nothing here is measured on the hosts, so without a firewall source the app cannot say anything about the network and shows nothing rather than guessing. Exposure on the other pages is unaffected: it is measured from how each process bound its socket.

An administrator configures the source in Riskability Configuration, Firewall data source: the index and field names, and the entry points (the internet, an admin network) that a route can start from. Until then every Network evidence row reads unknown, which is correct.

div.b: A firewall source is configured, but it yielded no permitted edges in the last 30 days.
div.span: Either the source holds no permitted flows yet, or the field mapping does not match the events. An administrator can run Test source on the Firewall data source page to see which. Nothing is drawn until an edge exists, because an empty graph and a quiet network look the same.

input.label: Show
input.choice: Jumps a CVE could help with

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_routeedges_lookup | stats count AS edges, dc(dst) AS hosts, max(walked_at) AS walked_at | eval walked = if(isnotnull(walked_at) AND walked_at > 0, strftime(walked_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "never")

panel.title: Possible jumps, as the firewall has seen them

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_routeedges_lookup | riskabilitywalk mode=view entry=$entry_filter|s$ host=$host_filter|s$ top=$top|s$ classes=$show|s$ | eval rk_p = split(ports, ",") | mvexpand rk_p | lookup riskability_routelisteners_lookup hostname AS dst, port AS rk_p OUTPUT packages AS rk_sw, rk_summary AS rk_sum | eval rk_sw = coalesce(mvjoin(rk_sw, ", "), "nothing the inventory knows of") | eval rk_line = "port " . rk_p . ": " . coalesce(rk_sum, rk_sw . ", nothing open") | eval rk_best_sw = if(rk_p == port, rk_sw, null()), rk_order = if(rk_p == port, 0, 1) | sort 0 src, dst, rk_order, rk_p | stats first(src_kind) AS src_kind, first(hop) AS hop, first(port) AS port, first(protocol) AS protocol, first(sessions) AS sessions, first(n_ports) AS n_ports, first(ports) AS ports, first(rk_class) AS rk_class, first(dst_mark) AS dst_mark, first(rk_total_hosts) AS rk_total, first(rk_shown_hosts) AS rk_shown, first(rk_hidden_hosts) AS rk_hidden, values(rk_best_sw) AS rk_best_sw, list(rk_line) AS rk_lines BY src, dst | eval rk_best_sw = coalesce(mvindex(rk_best_sw, 0), "unknown listener") | eval edge_label = protocol . "/" . port . " · " . rk_best_sw . if(n_ports > 1, " +" . (n_ports - 1), "") | eval edge_note = sessions . " sessions" . if(n_ports > 1, " over " . n_ports . " ports", "") . " · " . mvjoin(rk_lines, " · ") | eval edge_point = dst . " · port" . if(n_ports > 1, "s ", " ") . replace(ports, ",", ", "), edge_point_kind = "port" | eval source_kind = if(src_kind == "entry", "0:entry", (hop - 1) . ":host"), target_kind = hop . ":host" | eventstats max(hop) AS rk_maxhop, max(rk_total) AS rk_total, max(rk_shown) AS rk_shown, max(rk_hidden) AS rk_hidden | eval rk_labels = "c0:entry point,c1:hop 1" . if(rk_maxhop >= 2, ",c2:hop 2", "") . if(rk_maxhop >= 3, ",c3:hop 3", "") . if(rk_maxhop >= 4, ",c4:hop 4", "") . if(rk_maxhop >= 5, ",c5:hop 5", "") | rename src AS source, dst AS target, sessions AS value, rk_class AS edge_class, dst_mark AS node_mark | fields source, source_kind, target, target_kind, value, edge_label, edge_class, node_mark, edge_note, edge_point, edge_point_kind, rk_labels, rk_total, rk_shown, rk_hidden

viz.option: Nothing to draw for this choice. With "CVE-enabled jumps" shown, that means no observed jump from an entry point lands on a listener with a finding usable over the network; widen Show to see the rest. If every choice is empty, the walk has not run yet or edges exist but none from a declared entry point has resolved to a host and port in the inventory. Either no entry point is declared, or the addresses the firewall logged are not ones the inventory has seen a host hold. The Network evidence page's "where the app refused to name a host" panel says which.

html.div: Drawn from the walk at $walk_when$: $walk_edges$ observed jumps across $walk_hosts$ hosts. Showing $rk_shown$ of $rk_total$ hosts; $rk_hidden$ not drawn for this choice of jumps, host and cap. Each host-to-host jump is labelled with the port it landed on and the software listening there; a jump from an entry point shows its label on hover, since a fan of them would overprint. Hover any jump for every port and what is open behind each, click it for the findings.

div.span: CVE-enabled: a jump a CVE alone can make
needs a foothold: reachable, but wants credentials or a click
unrated: an open finding has no CVSS vector
permitted only: needs a zero-day or permissions
host reachable from an entry point on CVEs alone

div.b: A jump here is a permitted flow the firewall logged, and its colour is what an attacker would need to take it.
div.span: Every jump is graded from the open findings on the software listening where it lands, using the CVSS vector: reachable over the network with no privileges and no user action is CVE-enabled; reachable but wanting credentials or a click needs a foothold; and a flow onto a listener with nothing usable over the network is permitted only, which means the jump needs a zero-day or permissions the firewall knows nothing about. A red ring marks a host an attacker can reach from an entry point on CVE-enabled jumps all the way; the first jump of any other colour is where the CVE-only path stops. The software belongs to the jump, not to a column of its own: a chain through nginx, then PostgreSQL, then Kerberos names each on the jump that reaches it. Widths are sessions; a thin edge is still a path. CVE-enabled means possible, not proven: nothing here was exploited.

panel.title: Every path from an entry point, and what each jump needs

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_routepaths_lookup | eval rk_entryf = $entry_filter|s$, rk_hostf = $host_filter|s$, rk_show = $show|s$ | where rk_entryf == "*" OR entry == rk_entryf | where rk_hostf == "*" OR rk_hostf == "" OR isnotnull(mvfind(hosts, "^" . replace(rk_hostf, "\*", ".*") . "$$")) | where case(rk_show == "cve", full_cve == 1, rk_show == "cve,foothold,unrated", NOT match(flags, "P"), 1=1, true()) | eval rk_show = rk_show | eventstats max(truncated) AS rk_trunc, count AS rk_matching | sort 0 - full_cve, - jumps, - cve_run, - sessions_min, path_text | head 500 | eval Path = path_text, Jumps = jumps | eval "On CVEs alone" = case(full_cve == 1, "yes, every jump", cve_run == 0, "no, not even the first", 1=1, "the first " . cve_run . " of " . jumps) | eval "Where the CVE-only path stops" = stop_text, "Each jump" = each_jump | table Path, Jumps, "On CVEs alone", "Where the CVE-only path stops", "Each jump", rk_trunc, rk_matching

viz.option: No path matches this choice. With "CVE-enabled jumps" shown, only paths that stay CVE-enabled all the way are listed; widen Show to see where the others stop. If every choice is empty, no path starts at a declared entry point, or the walk has not run yet.

div.b: This list was cut by the walk's cap, so it is the worst paths, not all of them.
div.span: The hourly walk keeps at most two thousand paths, follows at most eight onward jumps from any host and stops one jump past the first that is not CVE-enabled. Everything it dropped is still in the jump list below and in the graph above; what it kept is ordered so the first rows are the ones that matter.

div.b: A path is CVE-enabled as far as its jumps stay red; the stop is the first jump that needs more.
div.span: Each jump is graded by the best open finding on any port the flow reached on the next host, so a path's grade is as generous as the weakest listener on the way. "Needs a zero-day or permissions" means the firewall allowed the traffic and nothing open at the far end is usable over the network: an attacker would need something the app does not know about. A path that is CVE-enabled all the way is still a possibility, not a demonstrated route.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where status="open" | eval rk_sel = $sel_node|s$, rk_kind = replace($sel_kind|s$, "^\d+:", "") | rex field=rk_sel "^(?<rk_host_of_port>.+?) · ports? (?<rk_plist>.+)$" | eval rk_port_rx = if(rk_kind == "port", "^(" . replace(replace(rk_plist, " ", ""), ",", "|") . ")$", null()) | where case(rk_kind == "host", hostname == rk_sel, rk_kind == "port", hostname == rk_host_of_port, 1=1, false()) | lookup riskability_exposure_lookup hostname, package OUTPUT port AS rk_ports | where rk_kind != "port" OR isnotnull(mvfind(rk_ports, rk_port_rx)) | join type=left hostname [ | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | where observed_grade IN ("confirmed observed", "historically observed") | stats values(port) AS rk_observed_ports BY hostname ] | eval rk_port_one = if(rk_kind == "host", rk_ports, "n/a") | mvexpand rk_port_one | eval rk_behind_observed = if(rk_kind != "host", 1, if(isnotnull(rk_observed_ports) AND isnotnull(mvfind(rk_observed_ports, "^" . rk_port_one . "$")), 1, 0)) | where rk_behind_observed == 1 | dedup finding_key | lookup riskability_aiverdicts_lookup cve_id OUTPUT priority_tier, priority_score, recommended_action, rationale | `riskability_cvss_reach` | eval "Over the wire" = case(rk_rank == 3, "yes, no foothold needed", rk_rank == 2, "yes, but needs credentials or a click", rk_rank == 1, "no CVSS vector", 1=1, "no, local only") | eval Tier = coalesce(priority_tier, "P" . case(severity=="critical", 1, severity=="high", 2, severity=="medium", 3, 1=1, 4)) | eval Score = coalesce(priority_score, ""), KEV = if(isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added != "", "yes", "") | eval Fix = coalesce(fixed_version, "") | eval "Why" = coalesce(rationale, "not analysed by the pipeline yet; tier from severity") | sort 0 - rk_rank, Tier, - Score | eval Installed = coalesce(current_version, last_version) | rename hostname AS Host, package AS Software, cve_id AS CVE, severity AS Severity, recommended_action AS Action | table Tier, Score, CVE, "Over the wire", Severity, KEV, Host, Software, Installed, Fix, Action, "Why"

viz.option: No open finding sits behind this point. For a host that means nothing open is behind a port traffic was observed to reach; for a port, nothing open on the software listening there.

div.b: Every row is an open finding the app already holds; nothing here is computed from the firewall.
div.span: The route says traffic was permitted to this point. These are the findings that were open on the software listening there, with the pipeline's tier where it has analysed them and a tier from severity where it has not. Over the wire reads the CVSS vector: the attack vector, whether privileges are needed, and whether a user has to act. A row that says "no foothold needed" is the one that makes a jump CVE-enabled; the rest sit behind the jump without opening it. A click on a jump lists the findings on the software listening on the ports that jump landed on; a host click lists only the findings behind ports traffic was observed to reach, not everything open on the machine. Clicking an entry point narrows the graph to it instead, since an entry point has no findings of its own.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_routeedges_lookup | eval rk_entryf = $entry_filter|s$, rk_hostf = $host_filter|s$ | where rk_entryf == "*" OR isnotnull(mvfind(entries, "^" . replace(rk_entryf, "\.", "\\.") . "$$")) | where rk_hostf == "*" OR rk_hostf == "" OR match(src, "^" . replace(rk_hostf, "\*", ".*") . "$$") OR match(dst, "^" . replace(rk_hostf, "\*", ".*") . "$$") | sort 0 hop, - rk_rank, - sessions | head 1000 | eval rk_p = split(ports, ",") | mvexpand rk_p | lookup riskability_routelisteners_lookup hostname AS dst, port AS rk_p OUTPUT packages AS rk_sw, rk_open AS rk_popen, rk_hop_class AS rk_pclass, rk_wire_text AS rk_pwire, rk_foot_text AS rk_pfoot | eval Kind = if(kind == "entry", "entry point to host", "host to host, hop " . hop) | eval Listening = coalesce(mvjoin(rk_sw, ", "), "nothing the inventory knows of") | eval Open = coalesce(rk_popen, 0) | eval "This port needs" = case(rk_pclass == "cve", "a CVE alone: " . rk_pwire, rk_pclass == "foothold", "a foothold first: " . rk_pfoot, rk_pclass == "unrated", "cannot say, no CVSS vector", 1=1, "a zero-day or permissions") | eval "Jump needs" = case(rk_class == "cve", "a CVE alone", rk_class == "foothold", "a foothold first", rk_class == "unrated", "cannot say", 1=1, "a zero-day or permissions") | eval "Last seen" = if(isnotnull(edge_last_seen) AND edge_last_seen > 0, strftime(tonumber(edge_last_seen), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "") | eval "On CVEs alone" = if(mvcount(dst_reach) > 0, "yes", "no") | rename src AS From, dst AS To, rk_p AS Port, sessions AS "Sessions, all ports" | table Kind, From, To, Port, Listening, Open, "This port needs", "Jump needs", "On CVEs alone", "Sessions, all ports", "Last seen"

viz.option: No jump has been observed from a declared entry point, and no permitted host-to-host flow resolved to two inventory hosts. The list is the walk's, at most a thousand jumps, worst first, one row per port each was seen on.
